task.description: This covers WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) together, combined into one dispatch since this is a documentation/repo-administration issue, not a code defect with an unknown root cause requiring separate exploration. Step 0.5: read docs/issues/*.yaml for entries with status: resolved whose description mentions branch protection or direct-push bypass -- confirm whether this exact gap has been seen before (ISS-0441 is the parent finding but is NOT a prior fix of THIS gap; it configured required-status-checks, which is a different mechanism than push restrictions). Step 1: confirm the finding first-hand, do not take ISS-0467.yaml's description on faith. Specifically: (1) Run `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow/branches/main/protection` and confirm the CURRENT live configuration -- specifically whether `restrictions` is still null today (0018's own record states it was configured null; confirm this has not changed since). (2) Determine what GitHub identity `git push`/`gh` currently authenticate as on this host -- run `gh auth status` and `gh api user --jq '.login'`, and determine whether that identity is a repository admin/owner (check `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow --jq '.permissions'`). This matters because the fix decision hinges on whether a 'restrict who can push' rule could actually distinguish a legitimate ORCH direct-action push (ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10's sizing rule) from an accidental/illegitimate bypass, given both would come from the exact same GitHub identity. (3) State plainly whether the same identity that would be exempted/restricted is the same identity ORCH already merges PRs as -- i.e. is there ANY identity distinction available on this project's current auth setup that a push-restriction rule could exploit, or would 'restrict to administrators' simply restrict to the one identity that already does everything, making it a no-op. Do NOT implement any fix or write to 0018/GIT_MERGE.md yourself -- produce ONLY the diagnosis in result.summary: the live-verified current state of `restrictions`, the live-verified pushing identity and its admin status, and an explicit factual answer to whether GitHub's push-restriction mechanism can distinguish the two push classes on this project as currently configured. This diagnosis is what CODE-DESIGNER will use to decide between option 1 (configure restrictions) and option 2 (documented prohibition in GIT_MERGE.md) -- do not pre-decide which option should be chosen, just establish the facts.

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup). Grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for restrict|push.*bypass|bypass.*push|direct.*push|branch.protection (-i): 7 hits -- ISS-0467 (this issue), ISS-0441, ISS-0440, ISS-0330, ISS-0230, ISS-0227, ISS-0080. Read the four non-obvious candidates in full. ISS-0330 ('requirement_status_invariants_test.exs A4b/A9 failures ... introduced by direct main push') is resolved, but it is a DIFFERENT gap: it diagnoses test-invariant fallout (missing agent: field, entries: count drift) from a direct push that landed content CI never checked -- it says nothing about GitHub's restrictions/push-restriction mechanism and does not touch 0018 or GIT_MERGE.md's merge procedure. ISS-0230, ISS-0227, ISS-0080 are unrelated (tenant-provisioning rollback, SandboxPool dead fields, a stale grep self-check) and only matched the grep on incidental words. ISS-0441 (resolved) is confirmed to be the PARENT finding per the handoff's own framing: it configured required_status_checks + enforce_admins:false, and its own record explicitly left restrictions: null and explicitly deferred this exact gap as a follow-up ('file a new issue recommending GitHub's restrict who can push ... be revisited, or that GIT_MERGE.md add an explicit line prohibiting direct pushes'). CONCLUSION: no prior resolved entry covers this exact gap (a direct git push bypassing required-status-checks via the silent 'Bypassed rule violations' path). This is not a recurrence of a fix that didn't hold -- it is the first time this specific mechanism (restrictions, as opposed to required_status_checks) is being diagnosed. Severity stays as filed (MINOR).

STEP 1 (diagnose, live-verified, not taken from ISS-0467.yaml's prose).

(1) Current live branch protection on main -- `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow/branches/main/protection` (run this session): returns 200 with body `{"url":"...","required_status_checks":{"url":"...","strict":true,"contexts":["Backend gate (mix letflow.check)","Frontend gate (npm run check)"],"contexts_url":"...","checks":[{"context":"Backend gate (mix letflow.check)","app_id":15368},{"context":"Frontend gate (npm run check)","app_id":15368}]},"required_signatures":{"url":"...","enabled":false},"enforce_admins":{"url":"...","enabled":false},"required_linear_history":{"enabled":false},"allow_force_pushes":{"enabled":false},"allow_deletions":{"enabled":false},"block_creations":{"enabled":false},"required_conversation_resolution":{"enabled":false},"lock_branch":{"enabled":false},"allow_fork_syncing":{"enabled":false}}`. There is NO `restrictions` key present in this response at all (GitHub omits it from the JSON when unset, rather than emitting `restrictions: null` literally) -- confirming 0018's own record (which configured it as `restrictions: null` in its PUT payload) has not changed: push/merge restrictions remain unconfigured today, exactly as 0018 left them and exactly as when ISS-0467 was filed.

(2) Pushing/merging identity -- `gh auth status`: `github.com / Logged in to github.com account tvolodi (keyring) / Active account: true / Git operations protocol: https / Token scopes: 'gist', 'project', 'read:org', 'repo', 'workflow'`. `gh api user --jq '.login'`: `tvolodi`. `gh api repos/tvolodi/letflow --jq '.permissions'`: `{"admin":true,"maintain":true,"pull":true,"push":true,"triage":true}` -- admin:true confirms this identity is a repo admin. Also confirmed `git remote -v` -> `origin https://github.com/tvolodi/letflow.git (fetch/push)` and `git config --get user.name/user.email` -> `Vladimir Titenko` / `tvolodi@gmail.com`: the same `tvolodi` GitHub identity is what both `git push origin main` (via the stored git credential/gh auth) and every `gh pr merge`/`gh api` call in this pipeline authenticate as. There is exactly one credential set on this host, used for every git and gh operation this pipeline performs, and it is a repo admin.

(3) FACTUAL ANSWER (not a recommendation): given this project's current single-identity auth setup, a GitHub 'restrict who can push to matching branches' rule (the `restrictions` field) CANNOT distinguish a legitimate ORCH direct-action push (the ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10 sizing-rule exception) from an illegitimate/accidental bypass push, because GitHub's `restrictions` mechanism operates at the granularity of WHO (which user/team/app) is allowed to push at all -- it has no concept of WHY a given push is being made, or of a per-push justification/attribution the way the required-status-checks + enforce_admins:false + `--admin` design in 0018 achieves for the merge path. Every push and every merge on this project comes from the exact same GitHub login (`tvolodi`), which already holds admin rights and is therefore the natural candidate for any 'who is allowed' allowlist. Configuring `restrictions` to permit pushes only from `tvolodi` would restrict push access to precisely the one identity that already does everything -- registering, dispatching, diagnosing, designing, implementing, reviewing, merging, and pushing directly -- making the rule a no-op with respect to distinguishing push classes: every push this pipeline could ever make, whether a correct sizing-rule direct-action push or an accidental/incorrect bypass of a red CI gate, originates from that same identity and would pass an identity-based restriction identically. This is a structurally different problem than the one 0018 solved for `gh pr merge`: that mechanism works because GitHub's merge-blocking on required status checks is orthogonal to WHO is merging (it blocks based on CHECK STATE, and enforce_admins:false plus the distinct --admin flag makes the admin's override a visible, separate, individually-logged act) -- but a direct `git push` to a protected branch has no equivalent check-state gate at all; GitHub's ONLY lever over a bare push is restrictions (who), signatures, and linear-history/force-push/deletion rules, none of which can gate on CI status the way required_status_checks gates a PR merge. So: `restrictions` cannot express 'block a push if required checks are not green' -- that is not what the field does; it only expresses 'block a push from anyone not on this allowlist', and on this project's current auth setup the allowlist and the set of everyone who ever pushes are the same one identity. CODE-DESIGNER should treat this as the deciding fact between the two options named in the issue: configuring `restrictions` would add a maintenance surface (an allowlist naming the one identity that already has access) without adding any actual discrimination between push classes, whereas a documented prohibition in GIT_MERGE.md (route every change, including trivial doc fixes, through the existing PR path that IS gated by required_status_checks) removes the alternate path entirely rather than trying to make it self-gating -- which is also the exact resolution 0018's own 'Follow-up, not re-opening this decision' note already anticipated.
